claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation into the FeNiCrCoCu coating can improve its overall wear resistance relative to an unchanged coating.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation.
The modified coating will retain the FeNiCrCoCu alloy system on a Cu matrix.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation is the structural mediator of the predicted wear improvement.
Intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates govern multi-type adaptive friction-interface protection.
Adaptive friction-interface protection produced by the nanohierarchical structure causes improved wear resistance.
The modified FeNiCrCoCu coating will have improved overall wear resistance compared with an unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating in matched tests.
The predicted benefit will persist from room temperature to 800 °C.
The predicted benefit will persist across varied contact regimes.
The exact relationship between the proposed architecture and wear resistance is not fully understood.
Wear rate and friction coefficient can be compared between the modified and unchanged coatings using sliding-wear tests under varied thermal and contact regimes.
Failure to obtain a significantly lower wear rate in the modified coating would reject the predicted wear-resistance improvement.
